annotations.text:
LAUDU enquiry flow

The contact section today is a mailto: link. That hands the visitor a blank email and no prompt, breaks on webmail and most phones, and delivers unstructured enquiries with no qualifying detail.

This replaces it with a three-step enquiry form, built in the existing LAUDU system — Dominique Black display, Neue Haas Light body, #E2231A accent, 2px radii, values lifted from assets/colors_and_type.css. Both artboards are clickable: type a bad email, tab out, and the real validation fires.

Fields — ask only what you need

Three required fields total: name, email, message. Everything else is optional chips.

Budget is optional and carries an explicit "Rather not say" — a required budget field on a studio site filters out the good enquiries along with the bad.

Each chip submits a stable value (asap, 1-3m, u10k) rather than its own label, so the desktop and mobile forms record the same answer even where the wording differs.

Validation — on blur, not on keystroke

Errors appear when you leave a field, clear the moment you fix them, and never interrupt typing.

Continue is never disabled. A greyed-out button with no explanation is the anti-pattern; instead Continue validates, shows the errors, and moves focus to the first bad field.

Each error carries a warning glyph as well as red, so colour is never the only signal.

Keyboard and screen reader

Each chip group is a single tab stop with a roving tabindex; arrow keys move within the group and Tab leaves it. That is the expected behaviour for a radio group, and it keeps the tab order down to six stops rather than nineteen.

A radio is never un-checked by re-activating it, so every group carries its own opt-out instead — "Not sure yet", "Exploring", "Rather not say".

The live region announcing step changes and the success state is present in the DOM from first paint. A live region that mounts together with its text is usually announced by nothing at all.

Contrast — measured, not eyeballed

Three results from checking the palette in assets/colors_and_type.css against WCAG AA:

#E2231A on white = 4.68:1 — passes for body text as well as large. The section is white, so the signature red is unrestricted here.

#E2231A on the black footer = 4.23:1 — fails AA for body text; passes for large text only. Worth checking wherever the live site sets red on the dark surface at body size.

--fg-faint #A3A3A3 on white = 2.52:1 — fails badly. Fine for hairlines, never for text. Placeholders in this flow use --fg-subtle #6B6B6B at 5.33:1.

Error text uses --laudu-red-deep #B81810 (6.61:1) rather than the signature red, since it sets at 14px.

Mobile

Primary action is full-width and bottom-anchored, in the thumb zone. Inputs are 52px, chips and Back are 44px.

Inputs are 16px — below that, iOS zooms the page on focus.

No fake status bar or keyboard drawn: the real ones render on top.

One place I overrode the skill

ux-designer's modal-vs-page decision tree routes "multi-step workflow, short steps" to a modal with a stepper. I kept it inline in the section instead.

On a one-page site the contact section is the destination — the header CTA and #contact both scroll here. Interrupting that arrival with a modal adds a dismissable layer between the visitor and the thing they came for, and modal overuse is on the same skill's anti-pattern list. The stepper gives the chunking without the interruption.

Sizing: the primary action is 56px and nothing in the flow is under 44px. For comparison, the existing .l-link "Start a project" control works out at about 43.5px tall (10px text at the inherited 1.55 line-height, plus 14px padding top and bottom) — just under the 44px minimum.
